purpose: Country evidence register entry. Records official agricultural production, crop yields, producer-price index, census metadata and sector context. This is not a farm enterprise budget or calculator-ready profile.

evidence.topic: Official 2025 crop area, production and yield observations
evidence.source: Statistics Mauritius, Economic and Social Indicators Issue 1914: Agricultural and Fish Production, Year 2025

values.note: National mean; Statistics Mauritius reports 63.17t/ha in 2024.
Processed sugar output; not sugar-cane farm-gate production.
Area under cultivation, not harvested area.
FAREI data adjusted by Statistics Mauritius for selected backyard crops.
Includes multiple crop groups; use crop-specific rows below rather than this aggregate for a single crop model.

values.indicator: Total food crop area including covered cultures
Total food crop production including covered cultures

evidence.methodology: Transcribed from Statistics Mauritius Tables 1, 3.1, 5.1 and 5.3. Official 2025 values are provisional; 2024 values are revised.
caveats: 2025 crop values are provisional and may be revised.
Sugar cane yields vary sharply by producer category; do not apply the national average to every farm.
Food-crop aggregates are not a crop-specific enterprise yield.

evidence.source: Statistics Mauritius, Agricultural and Fish Production Year 2025, Table 5.1

values.note: Cucumber is a component of the wider creepers group; area 436.6ha and yield 19.7t/ha.

evidence.methodology: Crop-level area, production and yield copied from Statistics Mauritius/FAREI national tables. Covered-culture figures are reported separately and must not be mixed with open-field yields.
caveats: The official report identifies 2025 as provisional.
Some crop group labels aggregate multiple species; cucumber is included under creepers.
National averages do not substitute for region, variety, season and production-system-specific farm data.

evidence.source: Statistics Mauritius, Agricultural and Fish Production Year 2025, Table 5.2

values.note: Area 14.5ha; production 1,968.5t; cucumber is within creepers.
Area 123.0ha; mean yield 115.8t/ha across diverse crops.

evidence.methodology: Official covered-culture crop tables; Statistics Mauritius defines covered cultures as hydroponic and non-hydroponic.
caveats: These high yields apply to protected systems and cannot be applied to open-field production.
Small area denominators make some yields sensitive to crop mix and survey coverage.
No corresponding crop-specific protected-system budgets or capital depreciation data are included.

evidence.source: Statistics Mauritius, Agricultural and Fish Production January-June 2026

values.note: Sugar cane production was 43,228t over this period; 2025 comparable area was 284ha and production 23,399t.
Harvested area 4,344.9ha; production was 10.0% higher than first-half 2025.
Harvested area 63.6ha; production was 32.5% higher than first-half 2025.
Open field plus covered cultures; 11.8% above first-half 2025.
Includes imported and local slaughter; local beef rose from 7t to 33t.

evidence.methodology: Statistics Mauritius six-month production report; values are partial-year totals, not annual estimates.
caveats: Do not annualise six-month production mechanically.
Beef includes imported cattle slaughter; it is not a measure of domestic herd output.
2026 sugar estimate by Mauritius Chamber of Agriculture is 225,000t sugar, an industry estimate rather than realised output.

evidence.topic: Producer Price Index - Agriculture, second quarter 2026
evidence.source: Statistics Mauritius, Producer Price Index - Agriculture Q2 2026

values.note: March 2026 index was 96.2; monthly index decreased 2.3% to June.

values.indicator: Fresh vegetable producer price index change
values.note: Subgroup change over the quarter; carrot index decreased 54.6%, creepers 12.9%.
Up 2.3% from March; poultry +1.9%, eggs +6.0%, cattle +6.0%, milk +8.6%.
Based on final sugar price for crop year 2025-26; 12.3% below crop year 2024-25.

evidence.methodology: National Producer Price Index for Agriculture, base period January-December 2025=100; weights reference year 2023.
caveats: An index is not an absolute MUR/kg or MUR/tonne price.
The index is useful for trends and deflation, not as a stand-alone selling price input.
Current product-level price quotations and farm-gate unit values remain necessary for gross margin calculations.

evidence.topic: Agricultural Census 2024 metadata and survey scope
evidence.source: FAO Microdata Catalogue, Mauritius Census of Agriculture 2024; producer Statistics Mauritius

values.indicator: Census reference date for livestock headcounts
Household farms in Phase II sample
values.note: 8,200 Mauritius Island and 2,000 Rodrigues; about 42% of the estimated population of household farms.

values.indicator: Private households in Phase III sample
values.note: Sample represented about 3% of households on Mauritius Island and 22% on Rodrigues.

evidence.methodology: FAO catalogue metadata for the national 2024 census. Scope includes crop and livestock activity, labour, land tenure, crop production, farming type, mechanisation, livestock, marketing practices, agricultural loans and constraints.
caveats: The FAO catalogue page documents the census and metadata; it is not itself the full microdata results table.
Need to extract official final census tables/microdata before using farm-size, labour, livestock and marketing variables in the calculator.
The survey used complete enumeration for non-household holdings and sample enumeration for household farms and private households.

evidence.topic: Food import dependence and national agricultural structure
evidence.source: U.S. International Trade Administration, Mauritius Country Commercial Guide: Agricultural Sectors; IFAD Mauritius country context

values.note: Trade.gov reports USD1.6bn, approximately 24.4% of total Mauritian imports.
Broad food self-sufficiency estimate; not a crop-specific production ratio.
Unmilled and other wheat; import volume, not domestic production.
Imported maize used in feed supply chain.
IFAD reports Mauritius imports 77% of food requirements; figures differ by source and definition.

evidence.methodology: Trade.gov guide and IFAD country context; trade and food-system context only.
caveats: The 25% self-sufficiency and 77% food-import dependence statements are broad estimates from different sources and may use different definitions; do not combine them as exact complements.
Import volumes and trade values must not be treated as domestic farm output or farm-gate prices.

evidence.topic: 2025 crop-specific and livestock production verification plus 2026 first-half update
evidence.source: Statistics Mauritius, Agricultural and Fish Production Year 2025; Agricultural and Fish Production January-June 2026
caveats: 2025 national crop totals are provisional.
Statistics Mauritius notes food-crop data supplied by FAREI and adjusted for selected backyard production.
Livestock slaughter totals include imported animals; in 2025, imported cattle accounted for 2,175t of beef and local beef for 24t.
January-June 2026 values are partial-year observations and must not be mechanically annualised.

evidence.topic: 2024 Agriculture Census final summary and spatial coverage
caveats: Census holdings count excludes sugarcane- and tea-only holdings.
The official summary's district data should be extracted from detailed tables before building subnational budgets.
Headcounts are in thousands as displayed in the official summary.

evidence.topic: Producer price index and official market information system
evidence.source: Statistics Mauritius Producer Price Index Agriculture Q2 2026; FAREI Agricultural Production and Market Information System
notes: PPI-A is an index, not an absolute MUR/kg farmgate price.

FAREI APMIS is a government-supported portal advertising crop production/area and current retail/wholesale price access; extract and archive dated observations with units and market definitions before using.
APMIS front page was accessible, but the underlying live price table was not extracted in this batch.

strengths: Statistics Mauritius publishes 2025 crop-level area, production and yields, including open-field and protected systems.
2026 first-half production and Q2 producer price index updates provide recent context.
2024 Agriculture Census has broad coverage and documented sampling methodology.
National currency and official statistics sources are identifiable.
Batch 29 cross-checked 2025 livestock slaughter totals and 2026 first-half production; official 2024 Census summary provides island-level holdings, land and livestock estimates.
limitations: No current crop-specific MUR/kg farm-gate price table or dated district-level producer quotations were extracted.
No complete current crop enterprise budgets with seed, fertiliser, crop protection, labour, irrigation, energy, land preparation, packaging and transport costs were identified.
Protected and open-field yields differ substantially and must remain separate model profiles.
Sugar-cane producer revenue depends on cane/sugar pricing and producer category; a simple commodity price proxy would be misleading.
Some livestock slaughter statistics include imported animals and cannot be interpreted as domestic production alone.
District/municipal-area crop-level production and yields are not yet mapped; national values cannot be presented as district-level results.

missing_before_calculator_activation: Extract 2024 Agriculture Census final national and district tables for holding counts, crop area, livestock inventory, labour, marketing channels and mechanisation.
Obtain current dated farm-gate prices by crop, grade, location and unit; link them to the official PPI-A only as a trend cross-check.
Collect crop-specific input quotations in MUR for seed/planting material, fertiliser, crop protection, labour, land preparation, irrigation, energy, packaging and transport.
Build separate open-field and protected-culture enterprise budgets, especially for tomato, cucumber and sweet pepper.
For sugar cane, document producer category, cane pricing formula, harvesting/transport deductions, ratoon cycle and applicable support/subsidy arrangements.
Validate livestock farm-gate sale prices and distinguish domestic production from imported animals slaughtered locally.
Map all units, seasons, crop names and currency to the existing calculator schema and run regression and UI tests.
Extract detailed 2024 Census tables by district, Municipal Council Area, District Council Area, Municipal Ward/Village Council Area where published.
Retrieve current APMIS crop-specific price series and archive market, grade, date, unit, wholesale/retail and producer/farmgate classification.
Obtain dated MUR farm input prices and farmer-paid labour, machinery, irrigation, energy, packaging and transport costs.
Create distinct open-field, protected-culture, sugarcane and livestock enterprise budgets with regional/ island differences.
activation_recommendation: Keep Mauritius inactive until absolute dated farmgate prices, farmer-paid input quotations and tested enterprise budgets are available. Official 2025 national yields and 2024 island-level census evidence are strong enough for research and preliminary model design, but not for complete regional profit estimates.
